-60.98000,13.90000.name: Decision on LMO for FFP under Article 11 in the absence of domestic regulatory framework
-60.98000,13.90000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
-60.98000,13.90000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-118.76700,34.14800.name: LifeStart Fertility Center
-118.76700,34.14800.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Anita P. Singh, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-0.59882,52.29116.name: Pharmaron UK Ltd.
-0.59882,52.29116.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Pharmaron Beijing Co. Ltd. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.96616,56.46100.name: Dundee Fertility Associates
-2.96616,56.46100.state: Tayside Complete Health, 7, Commercial Street, Dundee, DD1 3DA
-2.96616,56.46100.company: Satellite clinic to TFP GCRM Fertility
-2.96616,56.46100.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to TFP GCRM Fertility. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-73.96479,45.42008.name: Charles River Laboratories Montréal ULC – Laval
-73.96479,45.42008.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, November 2024
-73.96479,45.42008.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, November 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-62.27266,-38.77238.name: Pregna Medicina Reproductiva
-62.27266,-38.77238.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.pregna.com.ar. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

19.90400,50.02900.name: Selvita
19.90400,50.02900.desc: A Polish contract research organisation running drug discovery programmes for international clients. Central and Eastern Europe now hosts a substantial share of the trials and preclinical work that Western regulators read, so the evidence base for approvals in one jurisdiction is increasingly produced in another, under a different oversight system.

113.26440,23.12910.name: Guangdong / Hainan primate breeding sector
113.26440,23.12910.desc: China’s primate breeding industry, which supplies a large share of the world’s research monkeys and restricted exports during the pandemic — causing shortages and price rises in American laboratories. Research capacity in one country turned out to depend on animal supply from another.

113.26440,23.12910.name: Guangzhou Wolbaki — mosquito production
113.26440,23.12910.desc: Rears Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes at very large scale for release, in the facility behind the Guangzhou trials that suppressed local Aedes albopictus populations. Wolbachia is a bacterium rather than an engineered gene, so these releases sit outside biosafety frameworks entirely while doing what a gene drive is meant to do — which makes them the closest thing to a precedent for the engineered version.

36.71800,-1.26370.name: Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organisation
36.71800,-1.26370.desc: Runs the trials behind Kenya’s engineered cassava and maize work, in a country that lifted a ten-year import ban on engineered crops in 2022 and then faced a court challenge over it. The research and the legal fight are happening at the same time, which is the usual position across the continent and rarely the one described.

115.46400,38.87400.name: Institute of Forest Biotechnology, Agricultural University of Hebei
115.46400,38.87400.desc: The laboratory that has published the longest-running field studies on the commercialised poplar, including a five-year assessment of effects on the arthropod community and soil bacteria around transgenic 741 poplar. Its reviews state the position plainly: nearly 22 insect-resistant poplar varieties have been approved for small-scale testing, environmental release or pilot production; efficacy differs between clones, larval stages and insect species; and expression of one Bt protein was significantly higher than another and varied with developmental stage and tissue. A perennial with a long growth cycle needs long-term assessment before commercial production — and here the commercialisation came first and the five-year study afterwards.
